title: Tenant Geo-fence Presets and Verifiable Proof Artifacts for Hosted Endpoints
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Background: Customers require deterministic control over where their Hosted API data is stored and how long it is retained. Current 'region pin' controls are ad-hoc and tied to per-endpoint settings; auditing evidence for customer attestations is manual and time-consuming. This ticket defines a tenant-level geo-fence preset model (predefined residency + retention bundles), a deterministic precedence model for overrides, and an automated evidence artifact pipeline that produces verifiable, signed proof bundles for compliance reviews.

Goals:
- Introduce tenant-scoped 'Geo-fence Presets' that combine: preferred region set, retention profile (data TTL for logs/requests/embeddings), and fallback policy (soft-fail vs strict).
- Provide API + Console surfaces for preset CRUD, preview of effective placement, and tenant override rules.
- Produce a machine-readable proof artifact (signed snapshot) whenever a tenant's preset is created/changed or upon scheduled evidence export. Artifacts are KMS-signed and contain request-level placement hashes + proof of retention policy assignment.
- Automate daily evidence bundles for customers with an option for on-demand export. Bundles should be tamper-evident and include human-readable summary + compact diff from prior export.

Scope (in):
- Tenant preset model and precedence engine (preset, endpoint-level pin, route-level override).
- Console flows: create preset, apply preset to tenant, preview effective placement and estimated cost/tokens affected.
- Hosted API: new headers for region-intent and retention-profile preview; server-side enforcement hooks.
- Evidence pipeline: signed daily bundles, on-demand export, S3-compatible delivery + download link in Console.

Out of scope: Dedicated capacity scheduling changes, on-prem installer changes, and full legal contract automation.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Preset vs ad-hoc per-endpoint pins: presets reduce UI/ops friction but require careful precedence rules to avoid surprising overrides. We will implement explicit precedence (endpoint override > preset > default) and show a preview modal.
- Soft-fail vs strict: default preset will be soft-fail to avoid service disruption for tenants during rollout; strict mode requires approval and security review.
- Evidence format: JSONL snapshot with per-request placement hashes + manifest. Trade-off: verbosity vs verifiability. We choose compact JSONL + manifest + signature to keep bundle sizes reasonable while enabling auditors to sample full datasets on request.

API surface (proposal):
- POST /v1/tenants/{id}/geo-presets - create preset (name, region_list, retention_profile_id, fallback_policy)
- GET /v1/tenants/{id}/geo-presets - list
- POST /v1/tenants/{id}/evidence-exports - enqueue on-demand export (format=compact|full)
- GET /v1/tenants/{id}/effective-placement?endpoint={id} - preview service that returns resolved region, applied retention, and cost delta estimate

Evidence artifact structure (summary):
- manifest.json (metadata: tenant_id, preset_id, created_at, version, signature)
- requests.jsonl (each line: request_id, timestamp, region_assigned, placement_hash)
- retention_manifest.csv (endpoint_id, retention_profile_applied)
- diff.txt (human readable diff vs last export)
- signature.sig (KMS-signed blob of manifest.json hash)

Acceptance criteria:
- Tenant can create/update geo-fence presets via Console and API; preset shows estimated cost/latency tradeoffs in preview.
- Precedence engine resolves effective placement deterministically and matches Console preview.
- Evidence pipeline generates daily signed bundles; on-demand exports produce a signed downloadable artifact within SLA (5 min for small tenants, 1 hour for large buckets).
- Security: artifact signing uses Customer-managed or Redwood KMS keys (configurable). Strict fallback presets require security_review_required=true and explicit opt-in.
- E2E tests and integration tests covering precedence rules, artifact generation, and download flow.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag behind tenant opt-in; default new tenants get 'soft-fail' presets.
2) Beta with 5 pilot tenants and manual evidence review.
3) Open to all tenants with Console education materials and migration tool to convert ad-hoc pins into presets.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Metric: percent of requests honoring tenant preset vs default (goal > 99% after 2 weeks).
- Time-to-export metric for on-demand evidence.
- Bundle size and generation time.

Open questions:
- Should we include per-request PII redaction prior to export by default? (security wants yes; UX wants optional)
- SLA for strict preset failures: what is acceptable customer-visible error rate?

Links to artifacts: confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Geo-Preset-Design; design mock: https://drive.google.com/design/geo-presets; proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4721
acceptance_criteria: 1) Preset CRUD works in API and Console; 2) Effective placement preview matches runtime assignment for sample traffic; 3) Signed evidence bundles are generated daily and on-demand with manifest and signature; 4) Rollout completed behind feature flag and beta customers onboarded; 5) Security review for strict mode is completed.

2025-03-01 - Diego Ramos: Drafted API surface and opened proto PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4721). Requesting API review from SDK owners. Eng note: on-demand export currently scoped to async job queue; ETA for small tenants ~4 mins in prototype.
